elaine: FYI we had a tenant restore failure overnight. Root cause: ephemeral KMS grant expired during a long-running restore (grant TTL was 1h, restore ran 2.5h). Requesting short triage + permanent fix.
omar: Oof. Which key/tenant? Any CloudTrail Decrypt AccessDenied events?
elaine: key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/ten-0a1b2c and tenant id tenant-88. CloudTrail shows Decrypt AccessDenied at 2026-04-12T03:41:02Z. Paste log excerpt: `KMS AccessDeniedException: Grant token invalid or expired`.
julian: We've used short-lived grants to avoid long-lived cross-account grants. But long restores (huge snapshots) need grant refresh or a refreshable workflow. Two mitigation options: 1) extend grant TTL to 24h for long-running restores with strict allowlist, 2) implement a grant-refresher that re-creates grants mid-restore using a bootstrap role with permission to create grants.
sec-ops-bot: Suggested canary: implement grant-refresher (idempotent) in staging, run a 3h synthetic restore and verify KMS Decrypt events continue with no AccessDenied. Also add CloudWatch metric for `KMSAccessDenied` filtered on backup key aliases.
omar: I'm leaning to the grant-refresher + Audit enforcement. Extending TTL increases blast radius. The refresher requires granting an internal service principal kms:CreateGrant and kms:RetireGrant on that CMK; ensure its IAM role is tightly scoped and audited.
elaine: We should also augment audit logs: add a field `restore.job_id` to every PutObject/Decrypt event in our internal logs so we can correlate KMS events with job lifecycle. If grant-refresh fails, auto-rollback restore with human-in-the-loop.
julian: Commands to prototype refresher (pseudo):
```bash
# create grant
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/ten-0a1b2c \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/grant-refresher --operations Decrypt --name "tenant-88-restore-<job>"
# retire when done
aws kms retire-grant --key-id alias/rd-backups --grant-id <id>
```
sec-ops-bot: Detection queries: lookup Decrypt AccessDenied where requestParameters includes tenant-88 or where logs have restore.job_id. Also alert if Decrypt AccessDenied occurs >0 during a restore job.
omar: I'll own the refresher prototype and the IAM hardening; julian will add restore.job_id telemetry and the alert rules.
elaine: Plan: staging run tomorrow 02:00 UTC with 3h synthetic restore. If green, roll to prod with restricted TTL grants only for allowlisted tenants performing long restores.
julian: Also add an SLO: any in-progress restore must have grant TTL >= remaining estimated time, otherwise fail fast with a clear error to the operator.
elaine: Good call. I'll open CHG and attach this thread. Thanks all.
